description_full: Super Group (SGHC) Limited operates as an online sports betting and gaming operator. The company provides Betway, an online sports betting and casino offering; and Spin, a multi-brand online casino. It operates in Africa, the Middle East, the Asia-Pacific, Europe, North America, and South/Latin America. Super Group (SGHC) Limited is based in Saint Peter Port, Guernsey.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 2K people. Revenue per employee of $674K ranks in the above the sector median among Consumer Cyclical peers, improving at 6%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $108K of free cash flow annually.
financial_summary: Super Group (SGHC) Limited is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $5.8B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 39% against a 10% cost of capital — a 29-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $294M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.50× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -16.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 32× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 69% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 11% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Cyclical median (8%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.39x).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-10.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 28% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 40% and a beta of 1.03, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.20 vs 5y 1.05), so read it loosely.
About $28.9M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 76% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades only 9% below its DCF fair value of $12.46, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 47%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $9.43 to $16.90 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Consumer Cyclical peers: P/E 14.0 vs 19.3 and EV/EBITDA 8.6 vs 11.2 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.1% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 9 covering analysts target $18.67 on average, 64% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 10.2% annual cash-flow growth, 2pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 39% clears the cost of capital of 9.9% by 29pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.87).
It converts 16% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 2.50x, but high accruals (-16.8% of assets).
ROE of 21% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $388.0M.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.5% over 3 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 14%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 10.4% on average.
Analysts expect 14.3% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 68.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 24%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (13 sales, net $5.8M sold).
It returns 2.2% a year to shareholders (1.8% in dividends).
Short interest is elevated at 18.9% of the float, 11.3 days to cover.
people: With about 2,726 employees, each generates about $674K of revenue, 1.8x the Consumer Cyclical median, and productivity has risen 5.5% a year.
That works out to $108K of free cash flow per employee.
